page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the c3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is bundled with 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed local disk access, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieves average results in single-core stress-ng (1617.89) and Geekbench single-core (1714.0) tests, as well as single-threaded gzip compression (26.36 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.39 GB/sec). However, multi-core performance is weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, recording 29.2 GB/sec for large-block reads and 22.26 GB/sec for large-block writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is particularly poor at 21.7 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the c3-standard-4-lssd is suited for workloads that benefit from local NVMe SSD storage but do not require heavy multi-threaded compute or high memory bandwidth. It performs adequately for static web serving, showing a throughput of 6.5 GB/sec, and light single-threaded tasks. However, it is less efficient for database operations, software compilation, or intensive multi-core processing due to its lower multi-core and memory benchmark scores. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dedicated vCPUs and bundled local NVMe SSD storage provides a balanced resource density for basic storage-reliant applications, though resource-heavy workloads may face performance bottlenecks.
